claims.text: Increasing local chemical short-range order creates nanoscale energy barriers for dislocations in single-phase high-entropy alloys.
The energy barriers produced by short-range order hinder dislocation motion.
Increasing short-range order elevates hardness and yield strength relative to a fully disordered state.
Rapid quenching from a solution-annealing temperature produces an equiatomic alloy with minimal short-range order.
Varying thermal-treatment temperature and dwell time can induce different levels or types of local chemical order.
Changing the post-treatment cooling rate can control the level of local chemical ordering.
Chemical short-range-ordered regions act as localized barriers to dislocation glide.
Greater short-range order makes the dislocation energy landscape more rugged and raises activation barriers for dislocation activity.
Greater short-range order reduces dislocation mobility through stronger pinning or nanoscale segment detrapping barriers.
Samples with higher short-range order will have approximately 10–30% higher microhardness than the disordered baseline.
Samples with higher short-range order will have approximately 10–30% higher yield strength than the disordered baseline.
Hardness and yield strength will correlate directly with the measured degree of short-range order.
A fully disordered solution-treated sample with minimal detectable short-range order can serve as the baseline.
The hypothesis is intended to apply primarily to nominally single-phase multi-principal-element alloys capable of appreciable local ordering.
Significant phase segregation or precipitation may overshadow strengthening caused by short-range order.
Grain-size changes and secondary phases may independently affect the measured mechanical properties.
Heat treatment can change the dominant type of short-range order and produce a dramatic change in dislocation-slip behavior.
If substantial measured changes in short-range order produce no corresponding change in hardness or yield strength, the proposed relationship is falsified.
